r7-fix1-verify.title: Verify defect-1 fix (line-boundary guard) by probe, not by reading
r7-fix1-verify.imperative: Independently probe _reject_newline against every splitlines() boundary character (\v \f \x1c \x1d \x1e \x85 U+2028 U+2029), embedded AND trailing, plus the empty string and legit long/unicode values that must NOT be rejected. Confirm end-to-end the U+2028 forged-status-line attack is rejected before any file write. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r7-fix1-verify.finding: FIX HOLDS. Independent probe (own script, not the implementer's test file) against 11 boundary sequences (LF, CR, CRLF, VT, FF, FS x1c, GS x1d, RS x1e, NEL x85, LINE SEP u2028, PARA SEP u2029), each embedded/trailing/leading -- all 33 combinations rejected by _reject_newline directly. Empty string, a 100000-char value, real unicode text (accented/CJK/emoji), a literal backslash-n ESCAPE (two chars, not an actual newline), space, and tab all correctly ACCEPTED -- no false FAIL introduced. End-to-end CLI probe with 4 boundary chars the implementer's own tests did NOT name explicitly (NEL, RS, form-feed, U+2029; their tests covered U+2028 only) confirms the forged-'- status: retired'-line attack is rejected pre-write, rc=1, zero files written in every case.

r8-fix2-verify.title: Verify defect-2 fix (write-phase atomicity) by forcing a failure, not by reading
r8-fix2-verify.imperative: Independently force a failure partway through a multi-file commit() (monkeypatch or equivalent) and confirm the store is byte-for-byte unchanged, including no stray temp files left behind. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r8-fix2-verify.finding: FIX HOLDS for its claimed scope. Independent probe (own script) forced an OSError on the FIRST staged write.write_text call of a 2-file commit: store snapshot byte-for-byte unchanged before/after, zero stray .tmp- files. This is the complementary case to the implementer's own test (which forces failure on the 2nd write) -- both ends of the staging phase are now clean. Also probed the DISCLOSED residual gap directly: forcing os.replace() itself to fail on the 2nd of 2 moves (after both stagings already succeeded) DOES leave the store mutated (the 1st move already landed) -- but leaves zero stray temp files (the cleanup-on-move-failure path works), and this exact residual is named and accepted in commit()'s own docstring as not fully atomic across N files absent a WAL, which EPISODE_STORE.md's markdown-in-git constraint does not provide. Judged non-blocking: (a) it is a materially smaller/rarer failure surface than the original defect (only the OS's own already-atomic single-file rename primitive can fail here, not an ordinary write, so real triggers are pathological -- permission change or directory deletion mid-run, not disk-full); (b) it is honestly disclosed, not silently claimed away; (c) the original BLOCK's demonstrated defect (write_text failures leaving earlier writes landed, easily triggered by disk-full/permission/lock) is fully closed.

r9-class-hunt.title: Independent hunt for the same invariant-mismatch pattern elsewhere
r9-class-hunt.imperative: Independently re-derive the implementer's sweep claim: for every place the writer validates, renders, parses, or compares (ID_RE, RUN_RE, FIELD_RE, ASSERTION_HEADING_RE, HEADER_RE, strip() semantics, unicode normalization, case handling), confirm no value can pass validation but render/parse back differently (round-trip write-then-parse identity). Record pass/fail with a finding; note any new instance found.
r9-class-hunt.finding: NEW INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS FOUND, lower severity, non-blocking (see consolidation). ID_RE/RUN_RE/FIELD_RE/ASSERTION_HEADING_RE/HEADER_RE were traced against actual construction and confirmed consistent (RUN_RE-derived episode ids always match ID_RE by construction; no case-folding or unicode-normalization anywhere in the module so no case/normalization mismatch class exists). BUT: create.mechanical.artifact-ref entries are the ONE free-text-ish field NOT run through .strip() before storage in _apply_create (every mechanical scalar, every assertion statement, history, and every retire field IS .strip()ed before being stored) -- while parse_episode() strips the WHOLE PHYSICAL LINE (line.strip()) before matching FIELD_RE. Demonstrated end-to-end: an artifact-ref value of ' some/path.md ' (leading+trailing plain space, not a splitlines() boundary char, so it passes _reject_newline) is accepted by the CLI (rc=0), rendered verbatim to '- artifact-ref:  some/path.md ', then re-parsed by parse_episode() as ' some/path.md' -- the TRAILING space is silently dropped. render(parse(text)) == text is FALSE for this input; the RoundTripTests suite does not cover an artifact-ref with edge whitespace so this slipped through. Root cause is the exact class named in the rework brief: the guard's definition of 'safe' (splitlines()-boundary-only) and the parser's actual behavior (line.strip()) disagree on a dimension the implementer's own sweep did not check (their sweep verified every value routes through _reject_newline, but did not check that every value is ALSO .strip()-consistent with what the parser does to the line). Distinct from the two BLOCK defects in severity: whitespace-only, one field only (artifact-ref), no forged line, no loss of semantic content (a path reference legitimately carrying meaningful leading/trailing whitespace is not a realistic scenario), does not violate any of C2-C8 by name. Mechanical one-line fix available: strip() each artifact-ref entry at construction time in _apply_create, matching the pattern already used for every other field.

r10-no-regression.imperative: Check the value != "" empty-string carve-out is safe elsewhere; confirm the staging/replace change did not alter behavior on any previously-working path; confirm the error-handling split did not lose error information. Re-run/re-confirm close criteria C2-C8 independently and confirm the retirement layout placeholder shape is undisturbed (not re-litigated). Record pass/fail with a finding.
r10-no-regression.finding: Empty-string carve-out is safe: every field that reaches _reject_newline with a legitimate empty value (the 3 optional retire fields) has no other way to smuggle content through an empty string by definition; every field where empty is NOT legitimate is already caught earlier by a separate not-value.strip() emptiness check BEFORE _reject_newline runs, so the carve-out is never the only thing standing between an empty required field and acceptance. Staging/replace change: full suite (1181 passed/2 skipped, exact match) plus my own targeted probes confirm no regression -- Option-A adapter file-move+delete path, dry-run path, and every existing write-path test still pass. Error-handling split loses no information: independently probed (own script) that a forced OSError('[Errno 28] No space left on device') surfaces in full via the new message ('error: write failed, store left unchanged: [Errno 28] No space left on device') -- framing improved (no longer mislabeled as a delta-read failure), detail preserved. Re-confirmed independently (not by reading the prior review): C2 both directions (own probe: mechanical name smuggled into agent_supplied correctly rejected; fixture reproduces the other direction), C3a/C3b (fixtures reproduce), C4 (my own atomicity probes plus AllOrNothingAtomicTests read+passing), C5 (grep: durable_root only in docstring), C6 (own probe: sibling assertion blocks + Mechanical section byte-identical across a dispute), C7 (all 3 fixtures present at exact paths), C8 (read _apply_retire: routes only through apply_retirement(), no inline file-move; RetirementSeamTests' Option-A flip test passing). Retirement layout placeholder confirmed undisturbed: _LAYOUT_ADAPTER = _LAYOUT_OPTION_B unchanged (grep line 398), both adapters still fully implemented, TODO(g4) markers unchanged -- not re-litigated, matching the original review's accepted ruling.
